Pibeseth
pih-BEE-seth
proper noun
Hebrew Pi-beseth, from Egyptian Per-Bast, “house of Bast”; the delta city of the cat-goddess, the Greek Bubastis.

Biblical Definition

Pibeseth, the Bubastis of the Greeks, was a delta city given over to the worship of the goddess Bast, her house and shrine. Ezekiel names her in the roll of Egypt's cities appointed to the sword in the day of the LORD's visitation: “The young men of Aven and of Pibeseth shall fall by the sword: and these cities shall go into captivity” (Eze 30:17). The strength of a city is her young men, and it is her young men the LORD marks for the sword; the pride of the Nile should fall in the flower of her age, and the city of the cat-goddess should go into captivity. So the prophet sets Pibeseth beside Aven, which is On the sun-city, that the two great seats of Egypt's idol-worship might fall together, the house of the sun and the house of Bast alike. Pibeseth preaches the day of the LORD upon the cities of Egypt. He has a controversy with the idol-cities, and His sword is whetted against their pride. No temple of the beast-gods, no multitude of young and strong defenders, can turn back the sentence of the God who lives. When His day dawns upon a proud and idolatrous city, her young men fall and her people go into captivity, that men may know the LORD is God, and the idols are nothing.

Webster 1828 Definition

Bubastis, the delta city of the cat-goddess Bast, whose young men should fall by the sword (Eze 30:17); a witness to the day of the LORD upon the idol-cities of Egypt.

PIBESETH, an Egyptian delta city, the Bubastis of the Greeks (Eze 30:17).

From Per-Bast, “house of Bast,” the cat-goddess.

A seat of idol-worship, set beside Aven (On) by the prophet.

Her young men appointed to fall by the sword, her people to captivity.

A witness to the day of the LORD upon the cities of Egypt.

Key Scripture

Eze 30:17 — "The young men of Aven and of Pibeseth shall fall by the sword: and these cities shall go into captivity."

Eze 30:18 — "At Tehaphnehes also the day shall be darkened , when I shall break there the yokes of Egypt: and the pomp of her strength shall cease in her: as for her, a cloud shall cover her, and her daughters shall go into captivity."

Eze 30:13 — "Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will also destroy the idols, and I will cause their images to cease out of Noph; and there shall be no more a prince of the land of Egypt: and I will put a fear in the land of Egypt."

Zep 2:11 — "The LORD will be terrible unto them: for he will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen."

Modern Corruption

The city of the cat-goddess Bast, appointed to the sword; it rebukes the idolatry of the beast-gods and proclaims the day of the LORD upon the proud idol-cities.

expand to see more

Pibeseth was the house of a beast-god, where men bowed to the image of a cat and kept festival to a creature they had made a deity. Egypt filled her pantheon with the shapes of beasts and birds, and Pibeseth was among the chief of these shrines. This is idolatry sunk to its depths, when the glory of God is changed into an image made like to fourfooted beasts and creeping things.

The LORD's answer is the sword and the day of visitation: her young men shall fall, and the city shall go into captivity. He has purposed to famish all the gods of the earth: “The LORD will be terrible unto them: for he will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place” (Zep 2:11). The beast-gods of Egypt could not save one youth of Pibeseth. Let men forsake the idols, however festive their worship, and bow to the living God, before whom every false god shall wither in the day of His terror.

Hebrew Roots

Pibeseth renders Egyptian Per-Bast, “house of Bast”; the Greeks called it Bubastis.

Pibeseth — Egyptian Per-Bast, “house of Bast.”

Bast (Bastet), the cat-goddess of the delta.

The Greek Bubastis, a great festival city on the Nile.

Set beside Aven (On) among the doomed idol-cities (Eze 30:17).

Her young men marked for the sword in the day of the LORD.

Usage

"The young men of Pibeseth shall fall by the sword."

"Pibeseth was the house of the cat-goddess Bast."

"The day of the LORD came upon the idol-cities of Egypt."
